title: Add interactive RAG checkpointing guide and snippet export examples
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: customers building long-running RAG workflows asked for better authoring ergonomics when iterating on multi-step playbooks. This PR adds a first-class docs guide and matching example code for: 1) checkpointing RAG playbook state (so authors can persist and resume sessions safely), and 2) exporting and importing authoring snippets (compact, portable JSON/YAML bundles) for sharing and CI-driven regression tests.

What this PR includes: an author-oriented narrative + quickstart that walks through: creating a checkpoint-aware playbook, running an interactive session in the local devcontainer, exporting snippets after each step, and importing them into a fresh session. The guide highlights best practices for telemetry (what to sample), privacy knobs (PII redaction examples), and recommended contract tests to prevent regressions. Also included are two runnable example artifacts (TypeScript and a tiny Node CLI) and a small docs-site component for embedding a live snippet runner sandbox.

Why unique: previous quickstarts focused on single-run examples; this guide targets iteration workflows and reproducible authoring, with explicit snippet export/import semantics and telemetry suggestions. The examples are intentionally compact so they can be dropped into existing developer sandboxes or CI.

Checklist: - [x] Add docs page: docs/playbooks/interactive-checkpoints.md - [x] Add example TS snippet exporter: examples/snippets/exporter.ts - [x] Add playground runner component: docs-site/components/snippet-runner.mdx - [x] Add devcontainer quickstart for local testing: quickstarts/interactive-playbook/devcontainer.json - [x] Add unit smoke tests for exporter CLI - [x] Run linter/docs build and fix issues

Notes: this PR is docs-first: none of the runtime surface changes are required to author or run the examples. Implementations use existing Redwood SDK APIs (no breaking surface changes). The telemetry recommendations reference existing console features and the Optimize toolkit suggestions.

Usage summary (authoring flow): 1) Start quickstart devcontainer 2) Run `yarn start:playbook` to open the interactive runner 3) Exercise steps and use the "Export Snippet" button to create a portable YAML bundle 4) Rehydrate in a fresh session with the CLI `redwood-snippet import bundle.yml` 5) Use the included smoke tests to assert output stability

Related: ENG-1281 (playbook iteration improvements), PM-342 (authoring UX), SUP-4123 (customer request from support), and design notes in docs/notes/rag-checkpointing.md.
